author: Maryland State Wire
title: Maryland man pleads guilty to selling guns and drugs to undercover officer
text:
← Back to the wire
Maryland man pleads guilty to selling guns and drugs to undercover officer
A Maryland man has pled guilty after selling guns and drugs during an undercover operation led by local authorities in Harford County. Robert William Garland faces up to fifteen years in prison when sentenced next January.
A Maryland man pled guilty on Oct. 7 in federal court after agreeing to sell firearms and drugs to an undercover law-enforcement officer in Harford County.
Robert William Garland, 33, of Elk Mills, admitted to possession of a firearm by a prohibited person as part of an undercover investigation into drug and firearms sales. The announcement was made by Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, along with Special Agent in Charge Charles Doerrer from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives; Alison M. Healey, Harford County State's Attorney; and Sheriff Jeff Gahler from the Harford County Sheriff’s Office.
According to his plea agreement, Garland was contacted by an undercover detective from the Harford County Drug Task Force in January 2025 regarding his intent to sell firearms. Garland agreed over the phone to sell three rifles and a crossbow for $3,000. He met with the detective at a shopping center parking lot where he transferred the rifles—wrapped in clothing—and other items including two large capacity magazines and a range finder into the detective’s vehicle in exchange for cash. Garland is prohibited from possessing firearms due to prior convictions.
Garland also offered various drugs for sale during these interactions. The detective arranged with him to purchase one ounce (28 grams) of methamphetamine for $350. On Feb. 5, they met again at a Royal Farms location where Garland delivered methamphetamine in exchange for payment.
Garland faces up to 15 years' imprisonment for possession of a firearm by a prohibited person; sentencing is scheduled before U.S. District Judge Adam B. Abelson on Jan. 26, 2027, at 10 a.m., though actual sentences are typically less than statutory maximums based on federal guidelines.
This case falls under Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), which aims to reduce violent crime through coordinated enforcement efforts among law enforcement agencies and community organizations.
The U.S. Attorney’s Office serves nearly six million residents across Maryland as part of the Department of Justice; it prosecutes federal crimes—including those involving firearms—handles civil cases on behalf of the United States government, collects debts owed to federal agencies or victims resulting from criminal offenses or civil judgments against individuals or entities found liable under law; employs more than 200 personnel across its divisions; enhances quality-of-life through justice administration; counts alumni serving prominent government roles—all according to, the official website.
